Rainmaker is pioneering a modern cloud-seeding system to increase precipitation, improve water availability, and address severe-weather challenges. We combine atmospheric science, weather-resistant UAS, radar and satellite observations, numerical weather prediction, novel sensing systems, and sustainable seeding technologies to design, operate, and evaluate precipitation-enhancement programs.

Research at Rainmaker is attached directly to operations. Our scientists and engineers collect proprietary observations, deliberately intervene in atmospheric systems, evaluate the results, and use what they learn to improve the next operation.

Rainmaker is hiring its first dedicated Machine Learning Researcher. You will establish how Rainmaker uses machine learning across the company: identifying the most valuable problems, determining which are ready for ML, building working models, and partnering with engineers and domain experts to turn successful research into operational systems.

You will not inherit a single predetermined model roadmap. The opportunity set includes forecasting supercooled liquid water and cloud-seeding opportunities, assimilating multimodal observations into estimates of atmospheric state, improving microwave-sounder retrievals, predicting hail, learning from intervention outcomes, and finding other high-leverage applications across research and operations.

 - Write research-quality software and build prototypes that software engineers can help productionize when an approach proves valuable.

 - Help Rainmaker learn from every operation, field campaign, new sensor, and intervention.

 - Communicate results and limitations clearly to scientists, engineers, operators, and company leadership.

**Description**
 AWS CloudWatch OpenTelemetry is hiring!
   

  

 Come build the next generation of cloud observability with us. Amazon CloudWatch gives every AWS customer a single platform to send, store, and query metrics from over 70 AWS services alongside their own application telemetry, using the OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) and Prometheus Query Language (PromQL). Our Seattle team owns the query execution and long\-term metrics storage systems that make this possible: the distributed query engine that evaluates PromQL expressions in real time, the storage access layer that serves reads across storage tiers, and the durable pipeline that compacts and indexes billions metric data points per day and keeps them queryable for up to 15 months. We serve customers who depend on CloudWatch to monitor production systems using Grafana, Prometheus, and other Prometheus\-compatible tools. The Seattle team is small, early, and still making the foundational architecture decisions that will shape this service for years. Engineers who join now will have a visible and lasting influence on what it becomes. Engineers who thrive here pair strong distributed systems instincts with the discipline to build for correctness and availability at AWS scale.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Design, implement, and test new features across our distributed query and long\-term metrics storage systems using Rust and Java, leveraging AWS services including S3, Kinesis, DynamoDB, and ECS.
* Operate and maintain a globally available 24x7 service that customers rely on to monitor, alert, and analyze their metrics in real time, identifying root causes of operational issues and applying permanent fixes.
* Collaborate with customers, stakeholders, and peers to understand requirements, influence our roadmap, and shape how millions of developers and SREs monitor their systems.
* Contribute to the full software development lifecycle — from design and code reviews to testing, deployment, and documentation — while mentoring teammates through constructive feedback.
* Evaluate new tools and approaches to keep our systems and practices current, making recommendations to the team on adoption and integration.


 A day in the life
   

  

 On a typical day you might root\-cause a customer query issue, release a new feature, consult with principal engineers on a hard architectural tradeoff, or design a solution to a storage or performance challenge you have never seen before. You translate customer requirements into designs, evaluate tradeoffs, and break work into incremental deliverables your team can ship. A strong community of principal and senior engineers gives direct feedback and pushes your thinking. You are surrounded by people who are passionate about observability and who believe there is still a lot of ground to cover in helping developers, SREs, and operators understand their systems.
   

  

**About The Team**
 The AWS CloudWatch OpenTelemetry team builds the query execution and long\-term metrics storage systems behind Amazon CloudWatch. We are a small, early\-stage team in Seattle making foundational architecture decisions that will shape this service for years. Our mission is to give every AWS customer a reliable, performant way to store, query, and act on their metrics using open standards like OTLP and PromQL.
   

  

 We invest in growing our engineers from day one — you will be paired with a buddy, work closely with senior and principal engineers, and build a personalized development plan with your manager. Our culture values knowledge sharing, constructive feedback, and an inclusive environment where every voice is heard.
